title: BLOCK-LOG2: block decoding saves one logarithm in time and copies

claims.statement: For every N>=2 and shift s,n=ceil(log2N),the single BLOCK-LOG2 algorithm of proof.md uses finite exhaustive recovery below n=2^48 and otherwise m=ceil(RLOG(n)^2),kappa=ceil(log2m)+1,base=ceil(n/(m+1)-m/2)+1,s0=kappa+1,dl=base+s0,H=base+m-1,L=floor(m/(4s0)),widths base+i+min(s0,floor((m-1-i)s0/L)),root1,Kc=8192(m+10u+100),Kp=8192(u+100),u=ceil(log2n),and the reproduced capped source/extractor,physical binary/radix/high-part instrument and full bootstrap/signed-near-parity/two-adic decoder. Under independent ideal copies whole-secret recovery succeeds with unconditional probability >=1-2^-8. All four worst-case branch bounds hold jointly,including errors,discards,retries and aborts. At n=1 logarithmic envelopes use their positive n=2 values; finite exhaustive copies <=N(n+10) affect only absolute outer constants. F(n)=n/(log2n)^2+(1/2)(log2n)^2. Total charged work O(n^3(log2n)^2 2^F(n)),including addresses,lookups,gates,bit operations,source costs and initialization; time growth index1. The generalized batch usesh unused top bits; b0=floor(log2n),Lblk=ceil(n/b0). Uniform modular score decoding of both odd and two-adic blocks and the reduced deterministic global acquisition cap are in Sections9..13. All four bounds hold jointly.
